func_802197D8_5D4CA8.title: Turn an actor toward its target object
func_802197D8_5D4CA8.summary: Steps an actor yaw toward the position of the target object stored at task +0x84.

parameters.name: task
parameters.description: Live actor task with its own model/object at +0x18 and a valid target object at +0x84.

parameters.name: turn_step
parameters.description: Native angular step parameter; the stepping amount is twice this value in the 0..1023 yaw space. Congo passes 1.

func_802197D8_5D4CA8.returns: 0 when the yaw is snapped to the target direction, 1 after a positive yaw step, or 2 after a negative yaw step. Congo checks zero before advancing its turn state.
behavior: Dereferences the target-object pointer at task +0x84 and reads its float X, Y and Z at object +0x08, +0x0C and +0x10. It forwards those values and turn_step to the coordinate-based turning routine.
The coordinate routine obtains the moving actor object from task +0x18 and computes direction from the X/Z difference. Yaw is the unsigned halfword at that object +0x16, wrapped with mask 0x3FF.

If the shortest angular difference is strictly smaller than twice turn_step, it snaps to the target angle and returns zero. Otherwise it takes a signed step of twice turn_step and returns 1 or 2 for its direction.
The Congo turn callback invokes this helper with turn_step 1 and uses its return value to decide when the next native state may begin.
cautions: Both task +0x18 and task +0x84 must identify initialized live objects. The native helper does not test either pointer for null before dereferencing it.
Invoke only with the file_12 code and the actor resources resident, normally from the actor native update context. Calling again advances yaw again.

The target field is an object pointer, not a player-task pointer. A temporary target substitution must have object-compatible float coordinates and stay valid for the entire call; do not replace unrelated global player pointers.
Preserve the native return value in hooks and wrappers; treating this as a void helper loses the turn-completion signal.
func_802197D8_5D4CA8.exampleExplanation: Forward the native result while advancing a live actor toward its current target. The wrapper rejects null pointers; the caller remains responsible for their native lifetime and loaded resources.

func_80038B98_39798.title: Queue a native audio command
func_80038B98_39798.summary: Queues a 16-bit native audio command with the wrapper default parameters.

parameters.name: cue
parameters.description: Native 16-bit command or cue ID. Congo battle music uses 0x003D.

func_80038B98_39798.returns: No return value. The wrapper does not report whether the queue accepted the command.
behavior: Masks the cue to 16 bits and forwards it to the underlying audio queue with both additional parameters set to zero.
The queue holds at most eight pending commands and suppresses duplicates only while they remain in that pending queue. A later call can enqueue the same command again.

Congo camera initialization starts unsigned-halfword task timer +0x8A at 30. During its opening callback, the timer value 25 queues music cue 0x003D exactly once before the rest of the intro continues.
Subsequent Congo intro callbacks do not repeat that music command. Advancing directly to a later intro callback can therefore bypass its original music transition.
cautions: Invoke at the intended native transition. Repeating a command every frame is not prevented by a persistent already-playing check in this wrapper.
The void return provides no delivery acknowledgment; preserve the native audio scheduler and queue lifetime.
func_80038B98_39798.exampleExplanation: Queue the verified Congo music command once. The caller supplies the transition lifetime; the native wrapper supplies its default queue parameters.

func_80023E94_24A94.title: Read an immediate transient event
func_80023E94_24A94.summary: Returns the masked bit for an event in the immediate transient-event bank.

parameters.name: event_id
parameters.description: Immediate event identifier, distinct from a saved progress-flag ID. Congo camera shake reads event 0x0B.

func_80023E94_24A94.returns: The stored masked bit, not a normalized Boolean. Event 0x0B returns zero or 0x08; compare the result with zero.
behavior: Reads the immediate byte-backed event bank also used by func_80023DF0_249F0 and func_80023E40_24A40.
Event 0x0B occupies bit 0x08 in the second byte. Native camera code tests the raw return for zero before entering or leaving the Congo shake callback.
Congo health processing may set event 0x0B repeatedly while HP is exactly 25, 20, 15, 10 or 5. Other event consumers can clear it, so a current bank read can differ from an HP-based inference.
cautions: Use result != 0 rather than result == 1. A set event can return a different power-of-two mask.
This bank is transient and has separate set/clear functions. Do not substitute saved progress-flag readers or infer its lifetime from boss HP.
func_80023E94_24A94.exampleExplanation: Normalize the raw event mask at the read boundary. This queries the live event without changing it or deriving it from health.

func_080009C4_6B3C64.title: Fade and remove a Congo spin ray
func_080009C4_6B3C64.summary: Runs an initialized Congo ray through its native fade and removal phase.

parameters.name: ray_task
parameters.description: Initialized ray task with a live parent root at +0xD0; the current scheduler task must be this ray.

parameters.name: ray_object
parameters.description: The ray object supplied by the native scheduler, normally task +0x18. Both callback arguments are consumed.

func_080009C4_6B3C64.returns: No return value is used by the native callback convention.
behavior: The ray initializer starts unsigned-byte color/opacity scalar +0xEC at 64. The growing ray callback selects this fade callback after observing parent root +0xE8 bit 0x80.
Clears parent root +0xE8 bit 0x80 and tracks one of four directional yaw offsets from the parent according to the ray variant.
Subtracts two from the ray scalar +0xEC, clamps it at four, and updates the corresponding native ray colors. At four, requests native current-task removal.
Selecting the fade callback is sufficient to begin fading an initialized ray. No additional fade initializer resets its opacity.
cautions: Keep file_29, the initialized ray object and its parent root live. This routine assumes the ray initializer has already established its native resources.
Removal uses the current scheduler-task pointer. Manually invoking this callback under another current task can remove the wrong task.
Do not reset +0xEC to 64 on repeated state observations; doing so restarts the fade and prevents normal removal.
The shared parent stop bit can be clear while a ray is already fading. The ray callback and remaining scalar describe its ongoing lifetime.
func_080009C4_6B3C64.exampleExplanation: Observe the remaining fade scalar during its normal native callback. The hook preserves current-task ownership and leaves removal to the original routine.

func_08008E54_6BC0F4.title: Update the Congo camera shake
func_08008E54_6BC0F4.summary: Applies Congo camera shake while immediate event 0x0B remains set.

parameters.name: camera_task
parameters.description: Initialized Congo camera task with its live native camera handle at +0xD0.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: Second scheduler callback argument. This routine saves it but does not otherwise consume it.

func_08008E54_6BC0F4.returns: No return value is used by the native callback convention.
behavior: The ordinary Congo camera selects this callback when immediate event 0x0B is set. It returns to the ordinary camera callback when the event is clear.
Compares squared distance between the local player and task camera-position fields +0x80, +0x84 and +0x88 with threshold 10000.
Uses the unsigned-halfword world frame at full system +0x3ADCE modulo four. Far target-Y offsets follow 30, 33, 30, 27; near offsets follow 10, 13, 10, 7.
Updates the native camera target and matrix, then clears byte task +0xDC. The shake phase follows the native world frame; it is not a once-only effect triggered by a health value.
cautions: Run in the initialized Congo camera context with the file_29 code and camera resources resident. This is not a generic camera effect helper.
The camera follows the local player and the current immediate event bank. Preserve its own task and handle rather than substituting a root actor or saved progress flags.
func_08008E54_6BC0F4.exampleExplanation: Identify the installed native camera state without replaying its update or changing the event bank.

func_8020D848_5C8D18.title: Stage room actor data and spawn definitions
func_8020D848_5C8D18.summary: Selects the current room's actor-data wave and stages its static actor spawn definitions.
behavior: Indexes the per-room metadata table at D_80231300_5EC7D0 with the current room id and resolves the actor-data file that supplies the room's actor instances.
Runs before the static actor initializers and is retried while the actor-data wave is still loading. A hook here precedes every static actor initialization for the room.
Each metadata record exposes the normal actor-instance array, the partitioned/proximity actor lists and the actor-data file id. A zero instance definition terminates a list.
The stage only reads the room tables; the per-instance actor initialization is performed later by func_80218A54_5D3F24.
func_8020D848_5C8D18.exampleExplanation: The entry hook observes the actor-data staging step and checks that the current room's actor-data record is present before the native spawn uses it.
cautions: The actor-data resources can be absent on early passes; retry from a later invocation instead of resolving segmented pointers before the file is loaded.
Read-only observation is safe. Mutating the room tables without the native list and backlink rules corrupts actor spawning.

func_80218548_5D3A18.title: Handle an actor reaching zero health
func_80218548_5D3A18.summary: Runs the native zero-health handling for an ordinary actor; the authoritative local death edge.
behavior: Entered only from the common health-zero path after func_80218350_5D3820 has consumed the final health point. Room unloads and distance culls do not call it.
Performs the generic death handling for an ordinary actor, including the reaction, counters, effects and removal bookkeeping.
The synthetic fast-hit bit 0x00040000 at actor +0x68 reaches this path after subtracting one health point, which lets an external source drive the real death without a native attacker pointer.
func_80218548_5D3A18.exampleExplanation: The entry hook observes the authoritative zero-health edge for an actor. The entry argument is established; a complete callable prototype is not.
cautions: This is not a universal boss completion signal; bosses such as Dharmanyo and Tsurami use custom remaining-health callbacks.
The task may be removed after this path; do not retain or dereference the actor pointer afterwards.

D_80231300_5EC7D0.title: Per-room actor-data metadata table
D_80231300_5EC7D0.summary: Table of per-room records that describe each room's static actor-data wave.
behavior: Indexed by the raw room id (D_800C7AB2). Each entry describes a room's normal actor-instance array, its partitioned/proximity actor lists and the actor-data file id that supplies the instances.
Read by the actor-data spawn stage func_8020D848_5C8D18. A null record or a not-yet-resolved actor-data file means the room's actor wave is unavailable and spawning is deferred.
The instance and list pointers are segmented and must be resolved through the active actor-data file id; they are not raw RAM addresses.
D_80231300_5EC7D0.exampleExplanation: The table is indexed by the raw current-room id; a null entry means the room has no actor-data record.
cautions: Index only with a valid room id; the table has no bounds checking.
Resolve the record's segmented pointers with its own actor-data file id. Resolving them with an unrelated or unloaded file faults.

func_80002F54_3B54.title: Run the game-over step
func_80002F54_3B54.summary: Advances the native game-over state machine that offers continue or goodbye, and returns to the start sequence on goodbye.
behavior: This handler runs while the main system step at full-system +0x3ADD4 is 0x0E. Native death paths select that step only when the runtime life count reaches zero, so it is the game-over screen rather than ordinary gameplay.

A substate byte at full-system +0x3ADD6 drives a five-value sequence: 0 marks the transition, 1 initializes the game-over overlay and its task, 2 starts that task, 3 waits for it to finish, and 4 performs the exit.

At the exit substate, the completion byte at full-system +0x3ADD5 chooses the outcome. The value 1 restores saved state and selects step 0x0B; any other nonzero value runs func_8000383C_443C to tear down the overlay and selects step 3.
Step 3 is the start/sequence step that loads overlay file 0x16, and it is also selected by the ordinary world-teardown path, so this exit returns to the title flow instead of resuming the room.

The handler is dispatched once per frame while step 0x0E remains selected. Redirecting a game over to step 3 requires the teardown call before the step change, exactly as the native goodbye branch does.
cautions: The completion byte at +0x3ADD5 and the substate byte at +0x3ADD6 are separate fields; changing the wrong one does not advance the handler.
Selecting another step without the native teardown can leave the game-over overlay and its tasks resident.
The overlay identifiers and substates here are specific to the game-over flow; this is not a general menu interface.
